# 10 — Raycasting module audit vs the wasm geometry stack

## Summary

RynthAi's `Raycasting/` (9 files, 5,830 lines) is a **self-contained, host-independent ray-LOS engine**: it opens `client_portal.dat`/`client_cell_1.dat` off disk itself (via a private `DatDatabase` BTree reader in the shared `RynthCore.TerrainData` assembly), parses collision geometry, and answers one question — *"is my attack path to target X blocked by a wall?"*. Only **one** of the nine files invokes the host, and only for three read-only position/pose queries. holtburger already parses the **same** DAT geometry (gfxobj/setup/envcell physics polygons + terrain) in `crates/holtburger-dat`, but for a **different purpose** — AC-faithful *sphere-swept* movement collision, not ray-LOS — and it exposes **exactly one** geometry query to JS (`terrainHeightAt`). No LOS/raycast is reachable from JS or wasm today.

---

**Prior-claim verification:** "only 2 of 9 call host, read-only position queries" → **directionally correct, refined**: 2 files *reference* the `RynthCoreHost` type (`MainLogic`, `TargetingFSM`), but only **`TargetingFSM` actually invokes host methods** — 3 call-sites, all read-only pose/position getters. `MainLogic` only passes the reference through. The remaining 7 files never see the host. `rg -c 'RynthCoreHost'` → `TargetingFSM.cs:7, MainLogic.cs:1`; `rg -o 'host\.'` → `TryGetPlayerPose` ×2, `TryGetObjectPosition` ×1.

**Hidden dependency (not among the 9 files):** `Vector3` and `DatDatabase` are declared *in namespace* `RynthCore.Plugin.RynthAi.Raycasting` but physically live in the shared `Shared/RynthCore.TerrainData/` assembly — `Vector3Helper.cs:3,11` (143 LOC, custom Z-up Vector3, explicitly "replaces System.Numerics.Vector3"), `DatDatabase.cs:5,17` (357 LOC, from-scratch `FileStream` BTree DAT reader), `LandblockData.cs` (336), `TerrainSampler.cs` (259) — **+1,095 LOC** the module needs. This is the C# analogue of holtburger's `holtburger-dat/src/archive.rs`.

## (b) Duplication analysis vs `holtburger-dat` / wasm

### What overlaps

| Capability | RynthAi Raycasting | holtburger equivalent | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| DAT BTree file reader | `DatDatabase.cs` (`FileStream`, `GetFileData`) | `crates/holtburger-dat/src/archive.rs` (1,014 LOC) | **Full dup** — two independent readers of the same `.dat` format |
| GfxObj **physics** polygons | `LandblockStructs.cs` GfxObj unpack, `GeometryLoader.LoadGfxObjMesh:1298` | `file_type/gfx_obj.rs:18` `physics_polygons` + `:19` `physics_bsp` + `:22` `drawing_bsp` | **Full dup** — same source records |
| Setup / part frames | `LandblockStructs.cs` Setup (`:298`), `TransformVolume:1524` | `file_type/setup_model.rs` (745 LOC) | **Full dup** |
| EnvCell (dungeon rooms) | `DungeonLOS.cs` envcell parse (`:176-311`) | `file_type/environment.rs` (`Environment::unpack`, used at `lib.rs:17718`) | **Full dup** |
| Landblock terrain heights | `ScatterSystem`/`LandblockData.GetTerrainZWorld`, `GeometryLoader.RaycastLandscape:812` | `terrain_subdiv.rs:triangle_height_in_cell` (exposed as `terrainHeightAt`, `lib.rs:31428-31465`) | **Full dup** — wasm already ships this exact query |
| Region/scene scatter | `ScatterSystem.cs` (RegionDesc `0x13000000`) | `file_type/region.rs` (2,093 LOC), `holtburger-scenery-bake` | **Full dup** |
| Ray↔AABB slab test | `BoundingVolume.RayIntersectAABB:236` | `spatial/physics.rs:ray_aabb_entry:190` (identical slab method) | **Full dup** |
| Möller-Trumbore tri test | `BoundingVolume.RayIntersectTriangle:354` | *not as a public ray API* — collision uses BSP (`physics.rs`) | Partial |

### What does **not** overlap (the gap)

- **RynthAi is ray-LOS; holtburger is sphere-collision.** RynthAi answers *"does a line/arc from me to the target hit a wall"* (`RaycastEngine`, arc trajectories with per-weapon velocity `TargetingFSM:40-43`). holtburger's geometry stack answers *"can a sphere of radius r stand/move here"* — `physics.rs:BspNode.sphere_intersects_cell:115` / `sphere_intersects_solid:183`, the 32-file `transition/` module (a decomp-faithful port of acclient `CTransition`/`SPHEREPATH`, `transition/types.rs:1-25`), `check_walkable`/`step_down` (`spatial/transition.rs:656`). **Neither the wasm nor any Rust crate exposes a "target blocked" ray query.** Only `terrainHeightAt` is a `#[wasm_bindgen]` geometry export (1 of 1,264 exports).
- **holtburger has no parabolic-arc LOS at all.** The bow/crossbow/atlatl/magic arc trajectory sampling (`RaycastEngine.IsArcPathBlocked`) has zero counterpart — it is bot-specific gameplay logic, not client physics.
- **three.js `Raycaster` (`scene3d/picking.js:338-655`) is NOT reusable.** It is Y-up screen-space mouse-picking against rendered entity meshes on layers 0/1 (`:346`), requires the full render scene resident, and is skipped entirely under `?nullRender=1` bot mode. It solves "what did the user click," not "is my shot blocked."

### Coordinate conventions — the "D3D Y-up vs AC Z-up" premise is partly mis-stated

| Side | Frame | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| RynthAi Raycasting | **AC Z-up** (native) | `worldUp = new Vector3(0,0,1)` (`RaycastEngine.cs:63`); `GlobalZ = LocationZ` altitude (`TargetingFSM.cs:20,216`); dungeon vertex transform keeps `PosZ` as altitude (`DungeonLOS.cs:438-447`). The module **never touches D3D** — the D3D9 island is `Maps/DungeonMapTexture.cs`, outside `Raycasting/`. |
| holtburger-dat / world / physics | **AC Z-up** (native) | `holtburger_common::Vector3` used throughout `transition/types.rs`; terrain slope `1.0 - normal.z` (`scene3d/terrain.js:659`); GfxObj vertices stored raw, no swap. |
| holtburger **render only** (three.js) | **Y-up** | `acToThree(ax,ay,az) → (ax, az, -ay)` (`scene3d/entities.js:3374`); `// AC is Z-up; three.js is Y-up. We rotate worldRoot` (`scene3d/index.js:11`). |

**Correction:** both collision stacks (C# ray engine *and* Rust DAT/physics) already agree — **AC Z-up**. The Y-up frame exists *only* in the three.js render layer, and it's D3D-heritage in name only (three.js WebGL, not D3D9). So a wasm-backed LOS API would need **no coordinate conversion** to match RynthAi's math; the axis mismatch is entirely a render-side concern that a bot LOS query never enters.

---

## (c) Recommendation

**Keep the C# `Raycasting/` module in the bot process. Do not port LOS into wasm/`holtburger-dat` for this integration.**

Rationale, in priority order:

1. **It is already host-independent.** 6 of 9 files touch neither host nor async boundary; the only host coupling is 3 read-only pose getters in `TargetingFSM` — trivially satisfiable by the web host's `TryGetPlayerPose`/`TryGetObjectPosition` shims (task-02/host-seam scope). The module reads DATs *off disk itself*, so it works **identically regardless of native-vs-web target** — the build box has the DATs; the bot process does too.
2. **The poll-vs-async inversion is sidestepped.** LOS is a synchronous, pure computation over cached geometry (`GeometryLoader` LRU caches, `MAX_LANDBLOCK_CACHE=20`). Keeping it C# means `IsTargetBlocked` stays a blocking call the bot brain already expects — no round-trip into the async wasm/JS event loop per candidate target (`FindBestTarget` loops over *all* candidates, `TargetingFSM:167-196`; per-target async awaits would be pathological).
3. **wasm cost is real and the payoff is thin.** Exposing LOS as new `SessionHandle` methods means bloating the wasm crate with the ray-vs-mesh engine (`BoundingVolume`+`RaycastEngine` ≈ 654 LOC of new Rust), plus an arc-trajectory subsystem holtburger doesn't have, *and* re-deriving the simplified bounding-volume representation from holtburger's BSP polygons (a semantic mismatch — see risk R3). "Single source of DAT truth" is the only upside, and it is weak here because the two sides consume the DATs for different geometric abstractions.
4. **Terrain height is the one clean reuse.** If anything is shared, replace RynthAi's `GetTerrainZWorld`/`RaycastLandscape` terrain path with wasm `terrainHeightAt` (`lib.rs:31428`) — it's already exported, already Z-up, already faithful. But that's an optimization, not a blocker; the C# terrain sampler works standalone.

**If** a future goal is byte-exact server-authoritative LOS (e.g., to match what the AC server would allow), the *right* wasm surface is not RynthAi's approximate bounding-volume ray but a thin `line_of_sight(from, to)` built on holtburger's faithful BSP polygons (`physics.rs`) — a **new** capability neither side has, and out of scope for wiring the existing brain.

---

## (d) Risks

| # | Risk | Severity | Detail |
|---|------|----------|--------|
| R1 | **Two DAT readers drift** | Med | `DatDatabase.cs` and `archive.rs` independently parse the same format; a DAT-version quirk fixed in one won't propagate. Mitigated by DATs being frozen retail data. |
| R2 | **DAT availability on web target** | Med | The web client streams geometry via `holtburger-resource-http`/wsbridge; the *bot process* running `Raycasting/` still needs a **local `client_portal.dat`+`client_cell_1.dat`** (`GeometryLoader.Initialize` searches install paths, `:79-118`). On a pure-browser deployment with no local DATs, the C# module can't initialize — LOS silently no-ops (`IsTargetBlocked` returns `false`/"not blocked", `MainLogic:72`, `TargetingFSM:66`). Must confirm the bot host box ships DATs. |
| R3 | **Abstraction mismatch if ported** | Med | RynthAi tests rays against **simplified** volumes (sphere/cylinder/AABB + fallback AABB when triangle mesh is incomplete, `BoundingVolume:344-348`). holtburger stores **exact** physics polygons/BSP. Porting would either lose RynthAi's tuned approximations (`RayLateralOffset=0.35`, arc velocities, 0.5m/0.3m self-hit skips `RaycastEngine:105`) or require re-deriving them from BSP — a rewrite, not a reuse. |
| R4 | **Silent-fail semantics mask bugs** | Low-Med | Every failure path returns "not blocked" (`try/catch → false` in `TargetingFSM:64-160`, `GetPlayerPosition:218`). If host pose shims return garbage on web, LOS degrades to *always clear* with no error — the bot fires into walls rather than crashing. Needs a health/telemetry signal. |
| R5 | **Coordinate assumption on pose input** | Low | `TargetingFSM` assumes `TryGetPlayerPose` returns `(objCellId, localX/Y/Z)` in AC landblock-local frame (`:206-216`). The web host must supply pose in that exact frame (Z-up, local 0–192m), **not** the three.js Y-up world frame. A shim that accidentally hands over `acToThree`-converted coords would corrupt every ray. Low because the wasm world state is natively Z-up. |
| R6 | **Terrain-reuse frame subtlety** | Low | If `terrainHeightAt` is adopted (per rec #4), confirm it expects **global** world X/Y (`lib.rs:31429` `world_x, world_y`) whereas RynthAi computes global meters as `block*192+local` — verify the origin conventions match before swapping. |
